app.name: MuxMultiTool

help.title: Help
help.intro: What each screen is for, in the order of the navigation rail. Nothing is re-encoded unless a screen says so: streams are copied as they are.

screens.files: Browse the media folders, select files by name or wildcard and read the per-stream report.
screens.streams: Tick streams to keep or drop, apply rules by language, codec or id, extract tracks to files or remux to another container.
screens.combine: Build one file from streams of several sources, such as subtitles from one file added to another, with a time offset per source.
screens.cut: Mark segments of one file on the timeline and export them losslessly, as separate files or joined into one.
screens.merge: Join files with identical codecs into one without re-encoding, after a compatibility check.
screens.crop: Crop black bars from H.264 and H.265 video without re-encoding; the bars are detected and can be dragged.
screens.images: Take snapshots, set cover art and make GIFs from a video, or turn a GIF into an MP4 or WebM.
screens.batch: Run one stream operation over every file of a folder that matches a wildcard, each file as its own job, with a dry run first.
screens.presets: Saved stream operations to apply to a file on the Streams screen or to a folder as a batch.
screens.jobs: Every operation that writes output, with its progress, its ffmpeg command and its log.
screens.settings: Appearance, this help, the version and license of this build, and the software bill of materials.

help.shortcuts: Screens with keyboard shortcuts list them behind their keyboard button; pressing ? on such a screen opens the same list.
help.command: The exact ffmpeg command is shown on each screen before anything runs, next to the preview of what the job will do, and again in the Command tab of a job on the Jobs screen.
help.log: The ffmpeg output of a job is in the Log tab of its details on the Jobs screen: click a job name to open them.

mode.keepHint: Export the segments; the rest is dropped.
mode.keyframeHint: Lossless: each part starts at the last keyframe before its start, so nothing after the start is lost and up to one GOP is added in front.
mode.normalHint: Lossless: each part starts exactly at its start; the picture joins at the next keyframe, so it can stay black for up to one GOP.
mode.smartHint: Frame-accurate: the frames around each cut are re-encoded with the source's codec, everything else is copied.
mode.smartChecking: Checking whether this file can be smart cut…
mode.smartSummary: Re-encodes ~{seconds} s around {points} cut points ({encoder}). The rest is copied losslessly.
